source_text: simplices, qui, aliis occupati negotiis, nihil de eruditione ceperunt, sola tamen fide ad Ecclesiam Christi pervenire curarunt, ne facile obscuris quaestionibus terreantur, sed credentes Deum verum conditorem esse hominum, indubitanter quoque teneant quia pius est, quia verax, quia iustus; atque hanc aestimationem de illa Trinitate servantes, quidquid audierint huic convenire sententiae, amplexentur atque collaudent: nec hoc eis ulla vis argumentationis evellat, sed detestentur omnem auctoritatem atque omnem societatem contraria persuadere nitentem
pass_a_gloss: Simplices, who, aliis occupati negotiis, nothing about/from learning ceperunt, alone nevertheless fide to church of-Christ pervenire curarunt, lest easily obscuris quaestionibus terreantur, but credentes God true founder to-be of-human-beings, indubitanter also teneant because godly is, because verax, because just; and this aestimationem about/from that Trinitate servantes, quidquid audierint to-this convenire of-the-position, amplexentur and collaudent: nor this to-them ulla vis argumentationis evellat, but detestentur every auctoritatem and every societatem contrary persuadere nitentem.

lemmas.lexica: LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: Simple people, who are occupied with other business and have acquired no learning, have nevertheless taken care to enter Christ’s Church through faith alone. They should not be easily frightened by obscure questions. Believing God to be the true creator of human beings, they should also hold without doubt that he is good, truthful, and just. Maintaining this understanding of the Trinity, they should embrace and praise whatever they hear agreeing with this judgment. No force of argument should tear this from them; they should reject every authority and association trying to persuade them of the contrary.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
